results.title: Iran says resumption of war would not change its stances
results.content: TEHRAN — Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that a potential resumption of war with Israel and the United States would not change his country's positions. The remarks come amid mounting U.S. and Israeli threats of renewed attacks on Iran, as U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday that Washington "may do another little Epic Fury," referring to the U.S.-Israeli campaign on Iran that began on Feb. 28. "Recently, there has been talk of a new war, but I am already thinking about the post-war period. Whether there is war or not, our policies remain the same," Araghchi said during a televised event in Tehran. "They have already done so twice and have seen the results. If they want to try again, they know they will achieve no different outcome from those of the past." results.title: Tech companies turn to religion to make AI moral, but it's not that simple
results.content: LOS ANGELES — As tech companies race to build the most powerful artificial intelligence, some are also asking how to teach a chatbot right from wrong. Their answer? Religion. “These are not questions a lab can answer,” Anthropic co-founder Chris Olah said earlier this year at the Vatican’s presentation of Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI. “They are questions traditions like yours have carried for millennia.” Amid this much-discussed turn to faith, there has been little public scrutiny surrounding what exactly these technology companies think religion is — and, perhaps more important, what they hope to get out of it. As executives sound the alarm about AI's destructive potential and debate the need to develop morally good models, they are increasingly seeking input from philosophers and faith leaders. results.title: Lee says Korea emerging as global economic leader on record current account surplus
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung said Sunday that Korea has emerged as a leading player in the global economy, citing that the country posted the world's second-largest current account surplus among major economies in the second quarter. The country's current account surplus reached $116.63 billion in the April-June period, trailing only China's $193.72 billion, according to International Monetary Fund (IMF) data available on the Bank of Korea's Economic Statistics System. "The Republic of Korea is now moving beyond being a country that follows advanced economies to become a leading nation shaping the global economic landscape," Lee wrote in a social media post, referring to Korea by its official name. Lee noted that Korea's current account surplus exceeded the combined surpluses of Germany and Japan. He also highlighted the achievements of Korean companies in global markets, particularly in semi

results.title: Uzbekistan marks independence day in Seoul, citing $8 bil. in Korean investment
results.content: Uzbekistan's Ambassador to Korea Alisher Abdusalomov emphasized the importance of further expanding bilateral trade and industrial cooperation between Uzbekistan and Korea at a reception marking the country’s 35th Independence Day and the 34th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. "President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's state visit to the Republic of Korea in September this year marked an important milestone in the development of the Special Strategic Partnership between our two countries," Abdusalomov said Wednesday. He also stressed how the inaugural Korea-Central Asia Summit outlined a long-term vision for cooperation across various fields. Highlighting that Korean investment in Uzbekistan has surpassed approximately 11 trillion won ($8 billion), with more than 700 Korean companies operating in the country, the ambassador expressed hope for Korean companies' active pa

results.title: Saudi Arabia reopens airport as attacks by Houthi rebels persist
results.content: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia — Saudi Arabia reopened its main airport for international flights, more than two weeks after deadly strikes by Yemen's Iranian-backed Houthi rebels knocked the facility out of service. Earlier Sunday, the kingdom said it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile and a drone fired by the Houthis. A massive Israeli military operation underway this weekend in the occupied West Bank — in response to an attack that killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three in Hebron on Friday — has displaced hundreds of Palestinians over the weekend and put major restrictions on Palestinian movement. It comes just days ahead of Israel's tense election on Tuesday, a vote widely seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s handling of the wars and the hard-right turn Israel has taken both domestically and on the world stage. results.title: 2 Koreans finish as runners-up at LPGA event on home soil
results.content: Two Korean players tied for second place at the LPGA Tour event on their home soil Sunday, with one blowing a four-stroke lead and another coming up short after a late push. Yuri Yoshida of Japan won the BMW Ladies Championship with a four-round total of 17-under 271 at Pine Beach Golf Links in Haenam, some 330 kilometers south of Seoul, after carding a four-under 68 in Sunday's final round at the par-72 course. Yoshida held off two Koreans, Ryu Hae-ran and Choi Hye-jin, by one stroke for her first career victory. Ryu started the final round holding a four-stroke lead at 17-under but shot a 73 on Sunday after a bogey-birdie-bogey finish. Choi, going for her maiden LPGA title in her 125th career start, had a chance to force a playoff but had her birdie putt on the 18th hole lip out for a par and a round of 69. results.title: [PHOTO] Honoring Václav Havel's legacy in Seoul
results.content: Guests pose at the “A Gathering at the Václav Havel Bench” event along Yangjae Stream in southern Seoul, Oct. 20, hosted jointly by the Czech Embassy in Korea and Seoul’s Seocho District Office to mark the 90th anniversary of the birth of former Czech President Václav Havel (1936–2011). At the bench, installed in May 2025, Czech Ambassador Ivan Jančárek, third from right, highlighted Havel’s enduring legacy of freedom and democracy, while Czech Centre Seoul Director Michal Emanovský, fifth from left, emphasized the bench’s role as a place for dialogue and mutual understanding. Seocho District chief Jun Sung-soo, fourth from left, noted Korea’s own history of safeguarding democracy and said the two countries’ shared values would serve as a strong foundation for deeper bilateral ties. results.title: POSCO's 1% Foundation supports veterans, students, local communities
results.content: POSCO Group’s 1% Foundation is expanding its community programs, supporting veterans with disabilities, providing hands-on science education for teenagers and funding employee-led projects to address local needs. The nonprofit foundation, established in 2013, is funded by employee donations of 1 percent of monthly salaries and matching contributions from their companies. As of last year, 38,017 POSCO Group employees participated in the foundation’s donation program. Since 2020, the foundation has provided advanced assistive devices to veterans, service members and firefighters injured in service, in cooperation with the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, which helps identify recipients and assess their needs. Devices provided so far include a robotic walking aid for a veteran who suffered paralysis of the lower body after a fall during military service and a prosthetic arm for an

results.title: [COVER STORY] Kim Jong-un's China trip reaffirms 'blood ties' as Beijing watches Moscow
results.content: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s trip to the Chinese border city of Dandong, made days before the anniversary of Chinese troops entering the 1950-53 Korean War, was aimed at reaffirming the historic blood ties between the two countries at a moment when Pyongyang’s alignment with Moscow has drawn Beijing’s attention, experts said. North's state-run Rodong Sinmun on Sunday reported Kim's visit to the Memorial Hall of the War to Resist U.S. Aggression and Aid Korea in Dandong the previous day. The state media repeatedly emphasized Kim's paying tribute to fallen Chinese troops, remembering their shared history of fighting alongside North Korean forces and preserving ties forged in blood. results.title: Police step up crackdown on fake uniforms ahead of Halloween
results.content: Police will launch a nationwide crackdown on imitation uniforms and equipment ahead of Halloween amid concerns that such items could be used to impersonate officers or disrupt police operations. According to the National Police Agency (NPA) Sunday, the weeklong operation will run from Monday through Nov. 1, targeting the production, sale and distribution of imitation police gear in cooperation with provincial and metropolitan police agencies. Under the current law, civilians who wear or possess official or imitation police uniforms or equipment face up to six months in prison or fines of up to 3 million won ($2,260). The crackdown follows concerns raised after the deadly 2022 Itaewon crowd crush, when people costumed in police uniforms were reportedly mistaken for actual officers, causing confusion and hindering rescue operations. results.title: AIA Life Korea hosts K-pop concert for customers, employees
results.content: AIA Life Korea held a K-pop concert for customers, employees, their families and business partners from Korea, Malaysia, the Philippines and Singapore, combining Korean cultural performances with charitable giving, the insurer said Sunday. The "K-Pop Together, Give Together" concert was held at KINTEX in Goyang, Gyeonggi Province, Saturday, drawing around 7,000 people. The lineup featured Korean singers Jinusean, ITZY, J.Y. Park, Chung Ha and PSY, with actor Park Jae-min and singer Tiffany Young serving as emcees. Participants included members of AIA Life Korea and AIA Premier Partners, as well as AIA members from Malaysia, the Philippines and Singapore. The event offered an opportunity for attendees from across the region to connect through Korean culture. results.title: Netflix marks 10 years in Korea, unveiling new star-studded lineup
results.content: Netflix marked a decade of service in Korea with Netflix Janchi, a two-day fan festival held Saturday and Sunday in Seoul that brought together fans, actors, creators and executives to celebrate 10 years of Korean storytelling reaching global audiences. At the event, held at Oil Tank Culture Park in Seoul's Mapo District, key figures who led the global K-content phenomenon over the past decade through hit series such as "Squid Game" (2021), "KPop Demon Hunters" (2025) and "D.P." (2021) gathered to reflect on their journey as Netflix heralded a new leap forward for Korean original programming. During a panel looking back at iconic moments from "Squid Game" and sharing behind-the-scenes stories, lead actor Lee Jung-jae reflected on the cultural impact of the global phenomenon. results.title: North Korea's evolving threat goes beyond missiles as Russia ties deepen
results.content: North Korea’s military cooperation with Russia is giving Pyongyang more than new weapons. From electronic warfare equipment to battlefield lessons learned in Ukraine, the partnership could change how North Korean forces fight, military experts say, although the extent of those gains remains difficult to verify. Gen. Xavier Brunson, commander of U.S. Forces Korea, recently warned that North Korea had received Russian-made jamming equipment and had gained experience in moving troops and supplies over long distances through its involvement in Russia’s war against Ukraine. Speaking at a Center for Strategic and International Studies' event on Oct. 13, Brunson said the equipment marked a change in North Korea’s electronic warfare capabilities. “They didn’t have those jammers before. Those jammers were given to them by the Russians,” he said. Brunson also pointed to interference affecting move

results.title: Korean Air breach exposes blind spot in airline cybersecurity
results.content: A recent data breach involving Korean Air and Asiana Airlines demonstrates the aviation industry’s structural vulnerability to cyberattacks targeting third-party IT providers. Carriers depend on external IT system operators to manage critical operations, as they have to share passenger booking and ticketing data with external partners for real-time global operation. Last week, Korean Air and Asiana said customer reservation information had been leaked through Amadeus IT Group, a global aviation technology provider that operates reservation and ticketing systems for airlines worldwide. The two carriers said Amadeus had notified them of the incident on Tuesday. The breach is believed to have involved unauthorized access using login credentials assigned to an account in Amadeus' system. results.title: Korea's Q2 current account surplus tops Germany, Japan combined on chip boom
results.content: Korea’s current account surplus exceeded the combined total of manufacturing powerhouses Germany and Japan in the second quarter of this year for the first time since comparable data for all three countries became available in 1996, data showed Sunday. Booming semiconductor exports have pushed the trade surplus to record highs, while expanding overseas investments have boosted dividend and interest income. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) expects Korea's current account surplus to rank second globally behind China this year, with the largest increase among 190 countries. However, experts warned that a global slowdown in artificial intelligence (AI) investment or increased supply from rival chip exporters could threaten the gains, highlighting the need to diversify the country's industrial base. results.title: More Korean middle school students experience feelings of depression: data
results.content: The proportion of Korean middle school students who experienced feelings of depression exceeded that of high school students for the third consecutive year in 2025, data showed Sunday. The share of middle school students who said they felt depressed accounted for 26.2 percent last year, compared with 25.1 percent for high school students, according to the data by the Korean Educational Development Institute. In the study, "feelings of depression" were defined as experiencing sadness or despair severe enough to suspend daily routines for two consecutive weeks over the past year. In 2024, the proportion of such middle school students came to 27.9 percent, higher than 27.5 percent recorded for high school students. results.title: Nearly half of new Korean AI services based on Chinese foundation models
results.content: Korea's artificial intelligence (AI) development ecosystem is increasingly relying on Chinese foundation models, with data showing that nearly half of the models newly released by local developers this year were built on them, raising concerns that the country's AI industry could become technologically subordinate to China. According to a recent report by think tank Rockbridge Network Korea, Sunday, 49.3 percent of the 1,845 models published by Korea-based accounts on Hugging Face between January and August were based on Chinese models, compared with 35.9 percent based on U.S. models and 14.9 percent on domestic models. The share of new models built on Chinese foundations has been rapidly growing in past years, surging from 1.2 percent in 2023 to 22 percent in 2025, before nearly doubling this year. results.title: Footage released of huge Korean national flag on Dokdo Island
results.content: Promotional footage of a huge national flag of Korea on its easternmost island of Dokdo was unveiled Sunday to mark Dokdo Day, a social media post showed. A 30-by-20-meter Taegeukgi, unfurled by 70 Koreans at a pier on Dokdo Island, was captured in 60-second footage taken by drone, according to Seo Kyoung-duk, a professor at Sungshin Women's University in Seoul, on social media. The video also contained various images of Dokdo Island in the East Sea and a message recommending foreigners visit as part of a global promotional campaign for Dokdo. Korea has said Dokdo is historically, geographically and under international law its territory, categorically rejecting Japan's claim to the territory. Korea keeps a small police detachment on the islets, to showcase its effective control of Dokdo.

results.title: Foreign-language emergency calls more than double in Korea
results.content: As a record number of international tourists visit Korea, police are facing a growing demand for interpretation services, both for foreign-language emergency calls and at crime scenes. However, budget constraints have hindered efforts to recruit additional professional interpreters for languages other than English and Chinese, leaving officers to struggle with language barriers, particularly at crime scenes where interpreters are often difficult to secure on short notice. Foreign arrivals to Korea rose 21.5 percent year-on-year to 17.11 million in the first nine months of this year, up from 14.08 million in 2025, further increasing demand for police interpretation services. According to data submitted by the National Police Agency to Rep. results.title: Kim's China visit must lead to restraint
results.content: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s surprise visit to China is a reminder that the Korean Peninsula’s future cannot be understood through inter-Korean relations alone. Kim's crossing into Dandong via the newly opened New Amnok River Bridge and his meetings with senior Chinese official Wang Huning underscore the strategic importance Pyongyang attaches to Beijing. For South Korea, the appropriate response is neither alarmism nor wishful thinking, but rather a clear-eyed assessment of what closer ties between China and North Korea could mean for regional security, sanctions enforcement and diplomacy. The visit carried both historical symbolism and practical economic significance. Kim paid tribute to China’s participation in the Korean War and toured an automobile factory with Wang, who conveyed greetings from Chinese President Xi Jinping. results.title: Tigers slugger trying not to get caught up in numbers amid postseason surge
results.content: Kia Tigers slugger Kim Do-yeong claimed Sunday he never consciously tries to hit home runs, though it may not seem that way given the way he has swung the bat this fall. Kim slugged three home runs, including a massive grand slam, to help the Tigers sweep the defending champions LG Twins in the first round of the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) postseason last week. Those three home runs were Kim's only three hits of the three-game victory for the Tigers. Kim led the KBO with 45 home runs in the regular season and has picked up right where he left off in the postseason. The Tigers will continue their run in the second round against the Samsung Lions. Moments after the first game of that series was rained out in the southeastern city of Daegu, Kim said individual numbers can be dismissed in the postseason, where team wins matter far more. results.title: Incidents involving Koreans in 10 nations under travel advisory rise 50%: data
results.content: The number of accidents and incidents involving Korean nationals in 10 major countries under Seoul's travel advisory rose nearly 50 percent in 2025 from the previous year, data showed Sunday. In the 10 countries for which Seoul issued travel advisories the most over the past five years, the cases of accidents and incidents involving Korean nationals came to 4,016 in 2025, up 48.3 percent from 2024, according to the data from the foreign ministry and the National Police Agency to Rep. Kim Joon-hwan of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea. The countries are Russia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cambodia, Thailand, China, El Salvador, Mexico, Lebanon, Iran and Laos. Cases of losing contact saw the sharpest rise, increasing to 617 in 2025 from the previous year's 248, the data showed. Kidnapping and confinement more than doubled to 553 last year from 246 in 2024. results.title: Major banks plan bigger cybersecurity budgets for 2027
results.content: Major Korean banks are preparing to raise their information security spending next year following a wave of suspected artificial intelligence (AI) agent-driven cyberattacks and data breaches across the financial sector, industry officials said Sunday. Some intend to commit at least 100 billion won ($75 million) each to bolstering cyber defenses. The lenders have also launched urgent inspections and taken certain services offline to address a recently disclosed security flaw in PHP, a programming language used to build applications that process requests on web servers, including user logins and online posts. Hana Bank aims to earmark more than 100 billion won for information security next year, an increase of more than 50 percent from this year. results.title: Corporate watchdog chief calls for tougher penalties for obstructing investigations
results.content: Korea's antitrust chief on Sunday called for tougher financial penalties against companies that refuse to cooperate with investigations, following a recent dispute involving e-commerce giant Coupang. Ju Biung-ghi, chair of the Fair Trade Commission (FTC), said imposing fines equivalent to 1 percent of a company's total revenue for obstructing investigations would strengthen the watchdog's enforcement powers. "Imposing a fine equivalent to 1 percent of a company's total revenue for refusing to cooperate with an investigation, rather than a slap on the wrist, would strengthen investigative powers and make law enforcement more effective," Ju said in an interview with public broadcaster KBS. Ju said the FTC's existing investigative authority was largely sufficient, but stressed the need for tougher penalties against companies that refuse to cooperate. results.title: Brazil faces tense Lula vs. Bolsonaro runoff with US influence over Latin America at stake
results.content: RIO DE JANEIRO — Brazilians will choose between incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday's polarizing presidential election, a contest that will determine whether the U.S. will significantly expand its growing influence in Latin America. Polls before Sunday’s vote showed the two candidates, who need more than 50 percent of the vote to become Brazil’s next leader in January, in a neck-and-neck race. The election pits the left-of-center veteran politician Lula against Bolsonaro, an ally of U.S. President Donald Trump and the son of imprisoned former President Jair Bolsonaro. Flávio Bolsonaro bested Lula by more than 2.2 million votes in the first round of the election earlier this month. More than 33 million voters out of nearly 160 million abstained then. The difference between the two candidates is stark. Bolsonaro and Lula have opposing ideological vi

results.title: Korea to expand int'l flights in winter season
results.content: Korea will increase international passenger flights for the winter season, with more services to Japan and China amid strong travel demand, the transport ministry said Sunday. A total of 5,353 weekly international flights are scheduled on 264 routes connecting 44 countries during the winter season from Oct. 25 to March 27 of 2027, according to the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport. The flights will be operated by 84 airlines, including 11 Korean carriers and 73 foreign airlines. The weekly total marks a 7.6 percent increase from 4,973 flights during last year's winter season, surpassing the pre-pandemic level of 4,980 in the winter of 2019. The expansion will be driven mainly by additional services to Japan and China, with weekly flights increasing by 314 and 232, respectively, amid robust inbound and outbound travel demand.

results.title: See you later, alligator
results.content: When I was younger, kids and young people in the USA often said good-bye with the phrase, “See you later, alligator.” The other person would reply, “In a while (or after a while), crocodile.” There was no meaning implied using the terms for the oft scary reptiles of folktales (such as Peter Pan) and wild animal shows. Cultural differences emerged just the other day after a church fellowship meal, when I used the greeting with a young multicultural, English-fluent child. One of the Korean parishioners standing nearby called me out on my use of the term. He was worried the child might be scared or the parents may be offended. We launched into learning curves on all sides of the cultures in the room. The phrase is simply rhyming slang. There is no connection to reptiles. results.title: Lions reliever eager for shot at revenge in KBO postseason
results.content: Two years after his Samsung Lions lost to the Kia Tigers in the Korean Series, Lions reliever Lee Seung-min is still bitter about the experience. It was Lee's first postseason in the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO). He made two appearances and gave up a run in 3 1/3 innings, but the Tigers still prevailed in five games. This week, Lee and the Lions have their shot at revenge, as the two teams collide in the best-of-five second round starting Sunday at Daegu Samsung Lions Park in the southeastern city of Daegu. "After it all ended, I saw Kia players celebrate on the field, and I was pretty angry," Lee told reporters Sunday after practice. "I realized then nobody remembers who finishes in second place. results.title: Nat'l health insurance fiscal balance for foreigners tops $753 mil. in surplus last year
results.content: The fiscal balance of Korea's national health insurance for foreigners posted a surplus exceeding 1 trillion won ($753 million) for the first time last year, but the account for Chinese nationals swung to a deficit, data showed Sunday. The fiscal balance for foreign nationals came to 1,012.8 trillion won in the black last year, up from 943.9 billion won the previous year, according to data submitted by the National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) to Rep. Jeon Jin-sook of the ruling party. Insurance premium paid by foreign nationals totaled 2.54 trillion won, while medical expenses covered by the NHIS stood at 1.52 trillion won. It marked the first time that the health insurance fiscal balance for foreigners posted a surplus topping 1 trillion won. It also represented the consecutive surplus streak since 2017. results.title: KBO postseason game rained out
results.content: A Korean baseball postseason game scheduled for Sunday afternoon in the southeastern city of Daegu was rained out. The Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) postponed the first game of the best-of-five series between the Kia Tigers and the Samsung Lions at Daegu Samsung Lions Park in Daegu, some 230 kilometers southeast of Seoul, amid persistent rainfall. The game had been scheduled to begin at 2 p.m., but the league decided a few minutes after noon to push it to 6:30 p.m. Monday. During the postseason, all weekend games start at 2 p.m. and weekday games begin at 6:30 p.m. The winner of this series will advance to the Korean Series against the KT Wiz. Chris Paddack for the Lions and James Naile for the Tigers had been scheduled to start the first game, and their start will now come Monday evening instead of Sunday afternoon.

results.title: Chungnam National University holds town hall on future development plans
results.content: Chungnam National University held a town hall meeting on Friday to discuss its future development, including a proposed merger with another national university. About 250 people, including faculty members, staff, teaching assistants, students and alumni, attended the meeting at Baekma Hall of the university’s Jeongsimhwa International Cultural Center. The university said the meeting was organized to build consensus on major issues and future development plans, including a proposed merger with Kongju National University. Participants also discussed the Glocal University Project and a support package for flagship national universities, sharing their views on the university’s future. results.title: University of Seoul co-hosts Seoul Big Data Forum to explore new possibilities for data use
results.content: The University of Seoul held the 2026 Seoul Big Data Forum at Coex in southern Seoul from Oct. 6-7 to explore how artificial intelligence (AI) and big data technologies will shape future cities and open up new possibilities for data use. The two-day event was co-hosted by the Seoul Metropolitan Government, the Seoul Institute and the Seoul AI Foundation, the university said Friday. The forum brought together domestic and international experts to discuss advances in AI and big data and share their research findings. About 2,600 people, including AI, big data and robotics professionals, along with members of the public, attended the forum both in person and online. The keynote address was delivered by Dennis Hong, a renowned roboticist and professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, who directs the Robotics & Mechanisms Laboratory. results.title: Why Nepal's glacial lakes demand Indian action
results.content: Nepal’s ambitious six-year plan to drain four high-altitude glacial lakes — Thulagi, Lower Barun, Lumding Tsho and Hongu-2 — is born of sheer urgency. Following a catastrophic flood along the China-Nepal border that left more than 1,450 dead and thousands missing, Kathmandu is scrambling to mitigate future disasters. New Delhi cannot afford to view this as a purely domestic Nepali affair. For India, providing immediate technical support, data sharing and early warning systems to Nepal is proactive flood defense for its own northern plains. The catastrophic August deluge surged from the Lhende Khola into the Bhote Koshi, then wound through the Trishuli and Narayani rivers before crossing into India as the Gandak river to join the Ganga. results.title: Hyundai Motor, Kia's combined China sales fall below 10,000 units in Sept.
results.content: Hyundai Motor and Kia's combined retail sales in China fell below 10,000 vehicles for the first time this year in September amid sluggish demand, industry data showed Sunday. Hyundai Motor's sales plunged 47 percent on-year to around 4,000 units last month, while Kia's dropped 31 percent to 5,000, according to a Hana Securities report based on China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) data. Their combined sales fell 39 percent to approximately 9,000 units, with their market share slipping to just 0.6 percent from more than 10 percent in the mid-2010s. The automakers have struggled to revive sales despite introducing electric vehicles (EVs) tailored to the Chinese market. Hyundai's China-specific electric SUV Elexio sold just 251 units in the first nine months of this year, compared with 1,216 in the final three months of last year. results.title: Lotte steps up recruitment of Vietnamese workers
results.content: Lotte Group stepped up efforts to recruit local talent in Vietnam with a three-day campus recruitment event in Hanoi that drew more than 3,000 job seekers, the retailer said Sunday. The group held its 2026 Lotte Global Campus Recruiting in Vietnam for three days starting Wednesday at five universities in the Vietnamese capital, including Vietnam National University and Hanoi University of Science and Technology. Six Lotte affiliates operating in Vietnam — Lotte Department Store, Lotte Hotel, Lotte World, Lotte Innovate, Lotte Property & Development and Daehong Communications — took part in the event, offering recruitment briefings, career consultations and one-on-one mock interviews. Recruiters and current employees introduced their companies and job openings. They also shared practical advice on the application process and their work experiences. results.title: Foreign cruise ship visitors to Korea near 1.3 mil. in Jan.-Aug. period
results.content: The number of foreign visitors arriving in Korea by cruise ship neared 1.3 million in the first eight months of this year, driven largely by arrivals from China, data showed Sunday. A total of 1.28 million foreign passengers and crew members arrived aboard cruise ships in the January-August period, up 12 percent from a year earlier, according to the Korea Tourism Organization (KTO). With 148 cruise ship port calls and 638,905 passenger arrivals scheduled for the fourth quarter, the annual total could surpass 2 million this year, exceeding last year's record of 1.6 million. By port, Seogwipo on the southern resort island of Jeju accounted for more than half of all arrivals by sea through August. By nationality, Chinese citizens accounted for the single largest share at 57.7 percent over the period.

results.title: Tving tops new streaming app installations in September
results.content: New installations of Tving's mobile app rose for the second consecutive month in September, putting it back at the top of the video streaming app rankings despite controversy over a major personal data breach, industry findings showed Sunday. The Korean streaming platform recorded 814,483 new installations across Android and iOS devices in September, a monthly record and up 43.8 percent from 566,538 in August, according to Mobile Index, a mobile analytics platform operated by IGAWorks. The surge put Tving back in first place among streaming apps for the first time in three months. Tving previously topped the rankings in June with 451,491 installations, the month the data breach was first disclosed. Installations then plunged 24.6 percent to 340,409 in July amid growing concerns over the breach, sending the platform down to sixth place.

results.content: President Lee Jae Myung is mulling over selecting a justice minister nominee from between two prosecutor-turned-lawmakers after his previous pick for the post withdrew his candidacy last month over lobbying allegations, a source at the presidential office said Sunday. Rep. Park Kyoon-taek and Rep. Yang Bu-nam of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) are the candidates that Lee is reviewing for justice minister, a source at Cheong Wa Dae told Yonhap News Agency. "After a lengthy deliberation, Lee is reviewing the choice between Park and Yang. An official nomination is expected to be made soon," the source said. In a Cabinet reshuffle in late August, Lee nominated Rep. Kim Seung-won of the DPK to lead the justice ministry. results.title: Korea's temporary jobs fall to 31-year Q3 low
results.content: The number of temporary and daily workers in Korea fell to its lowest third-quarter level in 31 years amid a prolonged construction slump, government data showed Sunday. The combined figure dropped by 95,000 from a year earlier to 5.73 million in the July-September period, the lowest third-quarter level since 1995, according to an analysis of microdata from the Ministry of Data and Statistics. Of the total, the number of daily workers fell by 38,000 to a record third-quarter low of 833,000, largely due to weak employment in the construction sector. Daily construction workers declined by 28,000 to 381,000, accounting for 74.6 percent of the overall drop. Those in their 50s saw the sharpest decline, down 21,000. results.title: Montana's plan to curb election spending
results.content: One of the greatest frustrations I had during my 18 years representing the great state of Montana in the U.S. Senate was watching, in real time, the ever-increasing flood of corporate money poison our political discourse. Washington couldn’t — or wouldn’t — fix the problem unleashed by the Supreme Court’s 2010 decision in Citizens United, which allowed unlimited independent spending on elections by corporations and unions on free speech grounds. But now there’s a quiet revolution happening in the states that could finally take corporate money out of politics. And I’m proud that my home state is helping lead the way. results.title: CJ CheilJedang steams sticky rice for global expansion
results.content: JINCHEON, North Chungcheong Province — CJ CheilJedang, which introduced the country’s first microwavable steamed rice bowls under the Hetbahn brand in 1996 and has dominated the market since, is accelerating exports to promote healthier diets for global consumers. Hetbahn now exports to 60 countries, with the United States the largest market. The rice bowls were rebranded as Bibigo and entered the country in 2017. Across the world, Hetbahn last year saw its exports out of overall sales jump to 15 percent from 8 percent in 2021, with an average annual growth of 30 percent during the period. CJ CheilJedang is positioning rice as a “better carbohydrate” compared to bread as part of its global expansion. results.title: Ukraine says Starshield back to normal; Musk says Kyiv violated terms
results.content: KYIV — Ukraine said on Saturday that the Starlink satellite system and its military version Starshield were now fully functional after over a week of restrictions that disrupted military operations and intensified tensions with the U.S. But hours later, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, whose company owns Starlink, accused the Ukrainian military of violating the company's terms. Neither Musk nor the U.S. government, which operates Starshield using Starlink technology, had taken responsibility for imposing the curbs. "Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week," Musk said on X. Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov said on the Telegram app that the country is "physically unable" to use Starlink for long- and medium-range attack drone operations. results.title: NK leader vows to advance ties with China during surprise Dandong visit
results.content: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has visited China and vowed to promote the two countries' longstanding relationship forged in blood, state media reported Sunday. The report confirmed earlier accounts from South Korean government sources, who said Saturday that Kim visited the Chinese border city of Dandong, where he met with Wang Huning, China's fourth-highest-ranking official and chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. According to the North's Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), Kim visited Dandong on Saturday, accompanied by senior party and government officials, including Jo Yong-won, a member of the ruling Workers' Party's Presidium; Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui; and Kim Yo-jong, his sister and a party department director. results.title: Volunteers earn hours for future care as Seoul district pioneers exchange model
results.content: In the neighborhoods of western Seoul, an hour spent helping an elderly neighbor navigate a smartphone touchscreen could soon buy a ride to a hospital appointment or a helping hand with daily chores down the road. Seodaemun District is preparing to launch a local "time bank" system, allowing residents to earn time credits by volunteering and redeem them later for help from their neighbors. The ambitious initiative aims to transform the traditionally one-way dynamic of municipal welfare into a reciprocal, community-driven safety net. Under the framework, every hour a resident spends assisting someone in the community earns one hour of "time currency." Unlike traditional volunteer programs that draw a strict line between givers and receivers, the time bank operates on absolute equality: anyone can offer a skill they have and request support when they run into daily hurdles. results.title: N. Korean leader Kim Jong-un visits China to inaugurate a new cross-border bridge
results.content: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un visited China on Saturday, inaugurating a new bridge that connects the two countries and saying he hoped to expand cooperation with his powerful neighbor. Kim’s visit to China is his latest move in an increasingly assertive foreign policy as he seeks to align Pyongyang with Beijing and Moscow in a united front against the United States under what he portrays as a “new Cold War.” It's his first visit in a year. Kim arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong Saturday after crossing the newly opened bridge , according to South Korea’s Unification Ministry, which handles affairs related to North Korea, and China's official Xinhua News Agency. Both sides promised to strengthen cooperation He met with Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of China’s Communist Party. The two toured a car factory, and promised to strengthen the bilateral relationship.

results.title: Houthis attack Yemen's Aden, say Saudi strikes kill 16
results.content: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia — Yemen's Houthis said on Saturday they attacked the southern city of Aden, the interim seat of the Saudi-backed government, after accusing Riyadh of killing 16 people in strikes on capital Sanaa and a Red Sea port city. Saudi Arabia and the internationally recognised Yemeni government have come under sustained attack from the Iran-backed Houthis, shifting the focus of the wider Middle East war that erupted with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. The Saudi-led coalition said earlier on Saturday it had intercepted two missiles targeting Saudi cities Taif and Yanbu in the kingdom's west, before explosions were heard in Yemen's Aden, the home of the government that Riyadh supports in the years-long civil war. results.title: More than 400,000 protest across France, challenging Macron as Paris clashes erupt
results.content: PARIS — Clashes erupted in Paris as a mass march drew to a close Saturday, with more than 400,000 people rallying across France over school funding and soaring living costs in a fresh challenge to President Emmanuel Macron. Police made nearly 1,000 arrests, the government said. The Paris march began peacefully, a week after widespread rioting and looting during protests across the country. But near the demonstration's endpoint in eastern Paris, masked protesters hurled objects and fireworks at police, who answered with clouds of tear gas, deafening sound grenades and jets of water cannons. Officers with megaphones urged protesters to disperse. Some demonstrators panicked as tear-gas canisters landed in their midst, scattering with screams. results.title: Granddaughter of Korean independence fighter brings Korean history to US schools
results.content: At the first Korea Book Festival in Vancouver, Canada, which runs through Oct. 31, a very meaningful book was exhibited: "Jessie’s Diary," reborn as a graphic novel. On Oct. 8, a session was held where readers read the original work and shared their impressions, receiving a great response. The graphic novel has been introduced in French, Chinese and Japanese, and preparations are underway to publish an English edition of the original work as well. "Jessie’s Diary" is a child-rearing journal kept for eight years, beginning in 1938 with the birth of the couple’s eldest daughter, Jessie, by Yang Woo-jo (1897-1964) and Choe Seon-hwa (1911-2003), a husband and wife who participated in the Korean Provisional Government. results.title: Cattle farmers in Korea reeling from solar panel policy
results.content: At noon on Aug. 6 in a rural village in Naju, Jeonnam-Gwangju Special Metropolitan City, a thermal imaging drone camera showed the home and Korean cattle barn of Kim Young-hee, 73, and her husband, Lim Jae-yeol, 70, glowing red like a blazing heat island. Surrounded on all sides by three solar power plants that resembled a black sea, their home was trapped in the middle, with its roof surface temperature soaring to as high as 65 degrees Celsius.
